question: The value of sqrt{289}+sqrt{0.0324}-sqrt{7.29}=
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Memorizing squares up to 30 helps solve simplification questions instantly.

√289 = 17 (since 17² = 289)

√0.0324 = 0.18 (18² = 324; 4 decimal places in root reduces to 2)

√7.29 = 2.7 (27² = 729; 2 decimal places in root reduces to 1)

Value = 17 + 0.18 − 2.7 = 14.48

**∴ The correct answer is 14.48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

√289 + √0.0324 − √7.29

**Calculations:**

Converting the decimal values into fractions for easier extraction of square roots:

⇒ √289 + √(324 ÷ 10000) − √(729 ÷ 100)

⇒ 17 + (18 ÷ 100) − (27 ÷ 10)

⇒ 17 + 0.18 − 2.7

First, add the positive numbers:

⇒ 17.18 − 2.70

⇒ 14.48

**∴ The correct answer is 14.48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Decimals

When finding the square root of a perfect square decimal, count the total number of decimal places. The resulting square root will have exactly half as many decimal places. For example, 6 decimal places will result in 3 decimal places in the square root.

Fractional Method

Another reliable way to find the square root of a decimal is to convert it into a fraction using the rule √(a ÷ b) = √a ÷ √b. Example: √0.0144 = √(144 ÷ 10000) = 12 ÷ 100 = 0.12.

Important Squares to Memorize

For banking and competitive exams, memorizing squares up to 30 is crucial. Some key squares include 18² = 324, 24² = 576, 25² = 625, 27² = 729, and 28² = 784.
